solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Transubstantiationalist, for example, is one that's persistent!

definitions.meaning: a very lengthy word is an example of a ..., a long piece of vocabulary
lasting over an extended period, enduring

explanation.surface: A theologian who believes the bread becomes the body is praised as someone who keeps at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a joke: that monster of a word is literally a long term. Read as one compound, the same letters mean lasting a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something persistent goes on over an extended stretch, the everyday adjective sense of the compound.

clue.text: Trademark is piece of wood with circle

parts.note: a log is a cut piece of a tree trunk
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A company's mark is described as a ring with a lump of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem or symbol used as its trademark is commonly called by this short name.

clue.text: A bin I am moving around the country

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes themselves as a wheelie bin being trundled across a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-west Africa, so it fits the general description.

clue.text: International medics of present day: a mixed breed

parts.note: being present somewhere is being there, as in 'she was there'
a cross is an animal bred from two different breeds

explanation.surface: Seems to describe modern doctors as a mongrel sort of profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present day' looks like one phrase meaning 'now', but it splits: 'present' gives THERE and 'day' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the worldwide humanitarian organisation providing medical aid in wars and disasters.

clue.text: Odd characters from Rwanda, and not old Welsh county

indicators.note: take the first, third and fifth letters of the word that follows

parts.note: nor means 'and not', as in 'neither this nor that'

explanation.surface: Reads like a geography note saying something comes from Africa rather than Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd-placed letters of Rwanda are R, A, D. Radnorshire was a county of Wales before the 1974 reorganisation, also called Radnor.
explanation.definitionFit: Radnor, or Radnorshire, was a historic county in mid-Wales, abolished in the reorganisation of 1974.

clue.text: Has a cry of pain, and nauseous, extremely

parts.note: ow is what you shout when hurt

indicators.note: take only the letters at each extreme end of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in pain and feels sick at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to possess it, a straightforward synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Sound of fan, maybe, with his instantly recognisable rattle initially

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A football supporter is known by his distinctive rattle, waved at matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' suggests a football supporter with a rattle; it is the electric fan whose blades make a buzzing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirr is the continuous buzzing noise of spinning blades, as made by an electric fan.

clue.text: Skilfully avoid team on stage

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A squad stands on a theatre platform, dodging something deftly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem or tackle is to dodge it neatly, as a rugby player swerves past an opponent.

clue.text: Easy shot only some playing immediately

indicators.note: only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A golfer or tennis player is given an easy stroke if they start straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a gimme is a very short putt conceded without being played, so an easy shot.

clue.text: Turned to God, and yet unchanged on reflection

definitions.note: made into a god, raised to divine status

indicators.note: the clue's word must read the same backwards as forwards, as if seen in a mirror

parts.note: made into a god, raised to divine status

explanation.surface: Someone converts to religion yet remains the same person on thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' hints at a religious conversion; it means made into a god. 'On reflection' sounds like pondering, but describes a word whose letters read identically backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify someone is to make them a deity; the word is also a palindrome, the same reversed.

clue.text: How unfavourably (if also unclearly) to view things?

definitions.text: How unfavourably (if also unclearly) to view things?

parts.words: How unfavourably (if also unclearly) to view things?
parts.note: the phrase means seeing something unfavourably, and literally it means seeing in poor illumination, so unclearly

explanation.surface: A question about the pessimist's way of looking at the world.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for regarding something unfavourably also literally describes poor illumination that makes things hard to see.

clue.text: Capital city, so I see: urban sprawls

indicators.note: the letters of the words before spread out untidily into a new order

explanation.surface: A visitor remarks that the town spreads out in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina, a city famous for its huge urban spread.

clue.text: A volunteer army steal, if needs must

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
to pinch is informal for to steal

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers may resort to theft when circumstances demand it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an emergency or if absolutely necessary, matching 'if needs must'.

clue.text: Yon church's roof

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in 'yon hill'
CH is a standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Points out the roof of a distant church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roof' looks part of 'church's roof', but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is a roof covering of straw or reeds, so a roof of that kind.

clue.text: First date of the year, with north eastern girl

parts.note: January 1, written in the short form Jan I with a Roman numeral
NE is the abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A New Year's Day outing with a girl from the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Janine is a female given name, and crosswords often define names simply by sex.

clue.text: Barbecue would not be held here — nor is do, strangely

definitions.text: Barbecue would not be held here

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a barbecue would be out of place, and nor is a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' here is a party, part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbecues are outdoor cooking, so they would not take place inside a house or building.

clue.text: Thor loses nothing with wood hammer

indicators.note: the named piece is dropped from the god's name

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
ash is a kind of tree and its timber

explanation.surface: The Norse god lays down his famous hammer and uses a wooden one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like Thor's weapon, but it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer an opponent is to beat them heavily, the same as to give them a sound beating.

clue.text: Bird successfully dealt with by golfer getting labelled

parts.note: a pigeon is a bird
a golfer who sinks a putt has holed it

explanation.surface: A golfer hits a bird with the ball and is promptly branded for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pigeonholed is to be categorised or put in a fixed category, like being given a label.

clue.text: Germans long ago acquired High School

parts.note: got means obtained

explanation.surface: Historic Germans apparently bought a secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were ancient Germanic peoples who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Ancient language incorporated indefinite article

parts.note: Inc is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after company names
a is the indefinite article in English

explanation.surface: A grammar note: an old tongue absorbed the word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire's tongue, Quechua, is loosely called by the people's name, giving an old South American language.

clue.text: Girl has a tan after rambling

indicators.note: the letters of the words before are reordered, as if they had wandered about

explanation.surface: A girl comes back sunburnt from a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word for the walk, but it belongs with 'rambling' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a female given name, Russian in origin, so a girl.

clue.text: Right to get into dress that's got bigger

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the garment word

parts.note: a gown is a long dress

explanation.surface: The right person must squeeze into a frock that has become larger.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown, as in 'has grown', means increased in size, a synonym of 'got bigger'.

clue.text: A man's son making disapproving sound

parts.note: his means belonging to a man
S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A father's boy tuts at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences make a long sibilant noise to show disapproval, as when booing a pantomime villain.

clue.text: With ease, shifting very cold water

indicators.note: the letters of the words before move into a new order

explanation.surface: Something moves smoothly through freezing water.
explanation.definitionFit: The White Sea is an inlet of the Barents Sea in Arctic Russia, frozen for much of the year.
